simple.meaning: עָמַק (ʻâmaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be (causatively, make ) deep (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Psalms, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Hosea, beginning at Psalms 92:6. Its contexts include kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָמַק (H6009).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: to be (causatively, make ) deep (literally or figuratively)

occurrences.englishText: “Ask a sign of Yahweh your God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.”
Woe to those who deeply hide their counsel from Yahweh, and whose deeds are in the dark, and who say, “Who sees us?” and “Who knows us?”
For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.
The rebels are deep in slaughter;
